incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts for tenant CarobMed on dedicated-cluster us-west-2-dedicated-42. Start time 2026-03-15T02:07:14Z (ts: 2170001234). Error rate > 8% for 5m, p50 latency rising. Auto-page to #incidents and current oncall.

alex (oncall): Got the page, investigating. Can someone pull the per-route error breakdown and recent autoscaler events? :pager:

sarah (sre): Pulling logs now. Quick snapshot: gateway timeouts mostly to `/v1/stream` and a small % 502s on `generate`. NVGPU memory pressure on nodes in pool-dedicated-42, kernel OOMs show within last 10m.

mike (runtime): Confirming runtime metrics: GPU utilization at 98% on 3/5 nodes, long tail token generation sessions holding KV cache for >3k tokens. Queue depth spiking. Batching windows are enlarging and causing head-of-line waits -> gateway timeouts.

carol (solutions): CarobMed is running nightly summarization jobs around this hour. I just spoke to their support contact; they shipped a bulk backfill yesterday that could be still in progress. They have long-context requests (8k+).

ben (support): Customer impact: multiple 5xx and timeouts reported in their dashboard, some retries hitting rate limiter. They posted into their support channel. No PII reported, but SLA degradation.

alex (oncall): Initial mitigation steps: 1) throttle large requests for CarobMed at the gateway (reduce max_context to 4096) 2) temporarily reroute new requests to us-west-2-dedicated-43 3) scale up pool-dedicated-42 by +2 nodes if autoscaler lagging. I'll run commands.

alex (oncall): `redwoodctl tenant update-rate-limit --tenant carobmed --max-context 4096 --route /v1/stream`

incident-bot: Action queued: update-rate-limit job submitted (job id: j-9a7b).

alex (oncall): `redwoodctl cluster reroute --tenant carobmed --from pool-dedicated-42 --to pool-dedicated-43 --mode gradual --weight 0.3` — starting slow spillover to avoid double-saturating pool-43.

mike (runtime): Meanwhile I kicked off a scale: `k8s scale statefulset/dedicated-runtime --replicas=7 -n redwood-dedicated-usw2` (pool-dedicated-42 PV-backed nodes). Watching for new pods to register.

sarah (sre): Observability note: enabling debug trace for one of the heavy sessions to confirm KV cache thrash: `trace session-id 0x7fbd...` will add noise but helpful.

carol (solutions): Customer acked that they paused the backfill on their side. They asked if we can restore full throughput once stabilized.

mike (runtime): New nodes are provisioning; but I see one node failing pod init with `insufficient GPU memory` — looks like our scheduler attempted to co-locate a big batch job. I'll cordon the most saturated node and drain long sessions.

alex (oncall): `kubectl cordon node/usw2-d42-n3 && kubectl drain node/usw2-d42-n3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — draining now, will let pods reschedule to new nodes.

incident-bot: Notification: route throttle applied, reroute started, scale triggered, node cordon/drain initiated.

ben (support): Notifying CarobMed that we throttled large contexts and are moving traffic to another pool. ETA for stabilization ~10-15m. They appreciate the heads-up.

sarah (sre): After the reroute started, p50 latency dropped by ~200ms, error rate down to 3.6%. But we still see intermittent 502s from a single runtime process that hit a kernel OOM during model compilation path.

mike (runtime): Found the offender: a high-concurrency streaming job from a single API key that opens multiple simultaneous streaming sessions. It repeatedly requested length >8k with `stream=true`, keeping KV caches pinned. Blocking that API key for new sessions now.

alex (oncall): `redwoodctl api-keys block --key xxxxx-REDACTED --reason "excessive concurrent long-context streams" --tenant carobmed` — blocked new sessions.

carol (solutions): Customer says the job is a nightly transformer summarizer; they'll reconfigure to chunk and rate-limit. They asked for recommended config to avoid future saturation. I'll prepare a note: prefer chunked generation, smaller sequence windows, use dedicated reserved capacity for large backfills.

mike (runtime): After blocking key + reroute + scale, error rate stabilized under 0.5% and p95 latency returned close to baseline. No further kernel OOMs in the last 6m.

alex (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Will keep watch for 30m, then update status to resolved if stable. Please add any follow-ups.

carol (solutions): Follow-ups: 1) run a policy to auto-detect multi-stream bursts from single API key and auto-throttle 2) add autoscaler safety headroom for pools with night-batch schedule 3) customer-facing postmortem with recommended best practices for long-context jobs. I'll draft the note.

ben (support): Filing a support ticket with CarobMed summary and next steps; they'll want a timeline and confirmation when full throughput restored.

sarah (sre): Internal follow-ups: collect kernel OOM logs, node-level mem pressure trace, and confirm that KV cache evictions counted correlate with those sessions. I'll attach traces to the incident ticket.

alex (oncall): Thanks all. Good coordination. :thumbsup: Closing page in ~30m if stable.

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Metrics and timeline pinned to incident ticket IT-2170001234.
